label: Jamaica Hope

about.text: The Jamaica Hope is a dairy breed developed at Hope Farm in Jamaica for milk in the tropics. It is heat tolerant and tick resistant and was made from a Bos taurus by Bos indicus cross. It is fairly widely distributed on the island, with some 6,000 registered females.

links.name: Jamaica Ministry of Agriculture: Ja Hope Cattle brochure

sources.text: Hope Farm origin, heat and tick traits, Bos taurus x Bos indicus cross, 6,000 registered females and wide distribution from the Wikipedia article (found in WebSearch result text, page not opened). The brochure link is the Ministry's own document, found in WebSearch results (not opened).

Breeding started around 1910 at Hope Farm, and the animals were officially elevated to breed status in 1952; both from the Wikipedia article's text, found in WebSearch result text (page not opened). The FAO chapter was listed in WebSearch results and not opened.
Described as a dairy breed in the Wikipedia article's text, found in WebSearch result text (page not opened).

sources.text: Per-lactation range 2,102 to 2,390 kg: average lactation yields in a 1965-1973 FAO table, rising to 2,390 kg by 1968 (WebSearch result text, FAO page not opened). Lactation length 322 days from the Ministry brochure (WebSearch result text, not opened). Both figures are from the research summary and should be checked against the source pages.

facts.v: A 2007 Ministry of Agriculture presentation estimated an average annual yield of 2,540 litres for the national herd, and said productivity was 21 to 27 percent below the herd's potential.

sources.text: Found in WebSearch result text summarising the Ministry's 2007 presentation (not opened). Units are litres, not kg.

facts.v: Individual top cows reached about 9,000 to 9,300 kg in their best 305-day lactations.

sources.text: Attributed to FAO in WebSearch result text (page not opened).

facts.v: In 2024 the Ministry of Agriculture launched a project to safeguard the breed's genetic potential, aiming to raise milk yield, fertility and environmental adaptability.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article's text, found in WebSearch result text (page not opened).
